requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: no alternative of the alt statement could be executed in the actual snapshot
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism IS evoked at the end of each `alt` statement not annotated with the `@nodefault` modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.
requirements.original: The default mechanism is evoked at the end of each alt statement not annotated with the @nodefault modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the alt statement has the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism IS NOT evoked at the end of an `alt` statement annotated with the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: The default mechanism is evoked at the end of each alt statement not annotated with the @nodefault modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: An evoked default mechanism invokes the first altstep in the list of defaults, i.e. the last activated default, and waits for the result of its termination.
requirements.original: An evoked default mechanism invokes the first altstep in the list of defaults, i.e. the last activated default, and waits for the result of its termination.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default invoked by the default mechanism IS either successful or unsuccessful.
requirements.original: The termination can be successful or unsuccessful.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default IS unsuccessful if none of the top alternatives of the altstep defining the default behaviour could be selected.
requirements.original: Unsuccessful means that none of the top alternatives of the altstep (see clause 16.2.1) defining the default behaviour could be selected, successful means that one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default IS successful if one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.
requirements.original: Unsuccessful means that none of the top alternatives of the altstep (see clause 16.2.1) defining the default behaviour could be selected, successful means that one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement IS semantically equivalent to a nested set of `alt` statements, and the default mechanism applies to each of these `alt` statements.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: An interleave statement is semantically equivalent to a nested set of alt statements and the default mechanism also applies to each of these alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism applies to `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: This means, the default mechanism also applies to interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The restrictions imposed on `interleave` statements in clause 20.4 do not apply to altsteps activated as default behaviour for `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the restrictions imposed on interleave statements in clause 20.4 do not apply to altsteps that are activated as default behaviour for interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An alternative in an altstep activated as a default CAN refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Due to the possibility of defining dynamic test configurations, an alternative in an altstep activated as default may refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port belongs to the receiving component, and matching relates to the top elements of the port queues.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A dynamically unmapped or disconnected port contributes to a snapshot in the same manner as a mapped or connected port.
requirements.original: Dynamically unmapped and disconnected ports contribute to a snapshot in the same manner as mapped and connected ports.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep invoked as a default CAN execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped or disconnected ports without causing a test case error.
requirements.original: This means, an altstep invoked as default may execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.

ambiguity.issue: 'test case error' is a glossary term; the text uses it correctly but the receiving operations are elsewhere called 'reception statements'.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: In the case of an unsuccessful termination of a default, the default mechanism invokes the next default in the list of defaults that is not in the suspended state.
requirements.original: In the case of an unsuccessful termination, the default mechanism invokes the next default in the list that is not in the suspended state.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the last default in the list terminated unsuccessfully
requirements.canonical: If the last default in the list of defaults has terminated unsuccessfully, the default mechanism returns to the end of the `alt` statement in which it was invoked and indicates an unsuccessful default execution.
requirements.original: If the last default in the list has terminated unsuccessfully, the default mechanism will return to the place in the alt statement in which it has been invoked, i.e. at the end of the alt statement, and indicate an unsuccessful default execution.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the list of defaults is empty or contains only suspended defaults
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism indicates an unsuccessful default execution if the list of defaults is empty or contains only suspended defaults.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful default execution will also be indicated if the list of defaults is empty or if it contains only suspended defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: An unsuccessful default execution causes a new snapshot to be taken, or a dynamic error if the test component is blocked.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful default execution may cause a new snapshot or a dynamic error if the test component is blocked (see clause 20.1).

readings: After an unsuccessful default execution a new snapshot IS taken, unless the test component is blocked, in which case a dynamic error occurs.
After an unsuccessful default execution a new snapshot or a dynamic error MAY occur, at the discretion of the implementation.
ambiguity.issue: 'may cause' could be read as implementation freedom; clause 20.1 indicates the first reading (error only when blocked), which is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: After a successful termination, a default CAN stop the test component by means of a `stop` statement.
requirements.original: In the case of a successful termination, the default may either stop the test component by means of a stop statement, or the main control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement from which the default mechanism was called or the test component will take new snapshot and re-evaluate the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: After a successful termination of a default that does not stop the test component, the main control flow of the test component either continues immediately after the `alt` statement from which the default mechanism was called, or the test component takes a new snapshot and re-evaluates the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: In the case of a successful termination, the default may either stop the test component by means of a stop statement, or the main control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement from which the default mechanism was called or the test component will take new snapshot and re-evaluate the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: Re-evaluation of the `alt` statement after a successful default termination SHALL be specified by means of a `repeat` statement in the default.
requirements.original: The latter has to be specified by means of a repeat statement (see clause 20.3).

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the selected top alternative ends with break or without repeat
requirements.canonical: If the execution of the selected top alternative of a default ends with a `break` statement or without a `repeat` statement, the control flow of the test component continues immediately after the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: If the execution of the selected top alternative of the default ends with a break statement or without a repeat statement the control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language does not restrict the implementation of the default mechanism.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: TTCN-3 does not restrict the implementation of the default mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY implement the default mechanism as a process implicitly called at the end of each `alt` statement or as a separate thread responsible for default handling.
requirements.original: It may for example be implemented in form of a process that is implicitly called at the end of each alt statement or in form of a separate thread that is only responsible for the default handling.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the default mechanism has been invoked
requirements.canonical: When the default mechanism has been invoked, the defaults SHALL be called in the reverse order of their activation.
requirements.original: The only requirement is that defaults are called in the reverse order of their activation when the default mechanism has been invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` operation IS used to activate altsteps as defaults.
requirements.original: The activate operation is used to activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` operation has the syntax `activate ( AltstepRef ( [ActualPar {, ActualPar}] ) | ObjectReference )`.
requirements.original: activate "(" AltstepRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")" | ObjectReference ")"

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an AltstepRef
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an AltstepRef puts the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults.
requirements.original: An activate operation if it is called with an AltstepRef will put the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults and return a default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an AltstepRef
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an AltstepRef returns a default reference.
requirements.original: An activate operation if it is called with an AltstepRef will put the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults and return a default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS a unique identifier for the default.
requirements.original: The default reference is a unique identifier for the default and may be used in a deactivate operation for the deactivation of the default.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference MAY be used in a `deactivate` operation to deactivate the default.
requirements.original: The default reference is a unique identifier for the default and may be used in a deactivate operation for the deactivation of the default.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of a parameterized altstep that is activated as a default SHALL be provided in the corresponding `activate` operation.
requirements.original: The actual parameters of a parameterized altstep (see clause 16.2.1) that should be activated as a default, shall be provided in the corresponding activate statement.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'activate statement' although activate is an operation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of an altstep activated as a default ARE bound to the default at the time of its activation, not at the time of its invocation by the default mechanism.
requirements.original: This means, the actual parameters are bound to the default at the time of its activation (and not e.g. at the time of its invocation by the default mechanism).

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an ObjectReference re-activates the referenced default that was previously suspended by a `deactivate` operation.
requirements.original: If the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference, it will re-activate the referenced default which was previously suspended by a deactivate operation.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: A default re-activated by an `activate` operation with an ObjectReference SHALL remain in the same place in the list of defaults as before the `activate` operation.
requirements.original: In this case the referenced default shall remain in the same place in the list of defaults as it was before the activate operation, and the activate operation shall return with the same _ObjectReference as it received at calling._

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an ObjectReference SHALL return the same ObjectReference as it received at calling.
requirements.original: In this case the referenced default shall remain in the same place in the list of defaults as it was before the activate operation, and the activate operation shall return with the same _ObjectReference as it received at calling._

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The effect of an `activate` operation IS local to the test component in which it is called.
requirements.original: The effect of an activate operation is local to the test component in which it is called.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component CANNOT activate a default in another test component.
requirements.original: This means, a test component cannot activate a default in another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation MAY be called without saving the returned default reference.
requirements.original: The activate operation can be called without saving the returned default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: A default that is not explicitly deactivated IS deactivated implicitly at MTC termination.
requirements.original: This form is useful in test cases which do not require explicit deactivation of the activated default, i.e. deactivation of a default is done implicitly at MTC termination.

readings: Defaults not explicitly deactivated are deactivated implicitly when the MTC (and thus the test case) terminates.
Defaults not explicitly deactivated are deactivated implicitly when the test component owning them terminates.
ambiguity.issue: Defaults are local to each test component, so for a PTC the deactivation at 'MTC termination' is unclear; first reading kept as literal text. Also 'test cases' vs glossary 'test case'.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is activated as a default SHALL only have `in` formal parameters.
requirements.original: c) An altstep that is activated as a default shall only have in parameters.

readings: An altstep activated as a default SHALL only have `in` value or template parameters, apart from port and timer parameters, which are always passed by reference.
An altstep activated as a default SHALL NOT have any port, timer, `out` or `inout` parameters.
ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 3 (20.5.2-s024) activates an altstep with port and timer parameters, which are not `in` parameters; first reading chosen to stay consistent with the example.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `activate` operation SHALL be of `default` type.
requirements.original: d) The ObjectReference shall be of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `activate` operation SHALL refer to a default that is marked as suspended in the list of defaults.
requirements.original: e) The ObjectReference shall refer to a default that is marked as suspended in the list of defaults.

non_requirement.reason: introductory pointer to the general static rules of clause 5 / table 16; restrictions follow
